title: Technical design: settlement file landings into Kafka
subtitle: Custom S3 lister plus content hash. Not Debezium. Bucket s3://clh-settlement-prod/inbound.
author: Aman Kumar
audience: Priya Nair, Chris Patel, Kavya Menon, Marcus Bell, Helen Cho, Lena Ortiz
owners: Aman Kumar (lister and producer), Chris Patel (schema and late-file rules), Lena Ortiz (RailClear file contract)
summary: RailClear does not give us a database. Settlement arrives as files in s3://clh-settlement-prod/inbound, usually by 19:40 ET, sometimes after 20:00. This design takes those landings into Kafka topic clh.settlement.inbound with a custom lister and a SHA-256 content hash, then into ingest.raw_event. We are not using Debezium. There is no source WAL to tap. Later, if RailClear opens a replica, we can talk. Until then the file is the log. This document is the contract for schema, ordering, idempotency, and what happens when a file shows up after 8pm.
form_description: Technical design for Clearhaven settlement ingest. Written to freeze the lister-plus-hash approach and to kill the Debezium proposal before we spent a quarter on a connector with no source database.
revision_history: First draft after the file-drop vs Kafka memo kickoff.
Avro fields, late-file clock, hash collision notes.
Rejected Debezium section, ordering keys, failure modes.
Approved for build. Late cutoff stays 20:00 ET with a 02:00 ET salvage window.

blocks.text: 1. Decision

We will build clh-file-lister, a small service that lists s3://clh-settlement-prod/inbound, computes SHA-256 of each object, writes a Kafka record to clh.settlement.inbound if that hash has not been seen, and ignores the object if it has. Consumers downstream (ingest, then match-engine) already know how to read Avro from Kafka. They do not know how to watch S3. That is the whole move. We will not stand up Debezium. We will not ask RailClear for a database login this quarter. We will not parse files inside the lister. Parsing stays in ingest, where Chris already has the FIX-ish settlement layout and the tests.

blocks.label: Build this
blocks.text: Lister + hash in clh-file-lister. Topic clh.settlement.inbound, 24 partitions, key = settlement_dt + '|' + filename. Idempotency store in ingest.file_index (hash primary key). Late files after 20:00 ET still land; they get late=true and Helen pages if they arrive after 02:00 ET next calendar day. Target: first prod file through Kafka by March 3, 2023.

blocks.label: Not in this design
blocks.text: No Debezium. No S3 event notification as the only trigger (we use it as a hint, we still list). No Lambda per object. No 'just keep the nightly rsync to the NAS and skip Kafka' which is what we do today and what the recon platform design already said we would leave.

Marcus wanted a date for when we stop reading the NAS share entirely. That is not this document. This document gets files into Kafka without lying about order. Cutting the NAS is a cutover SOP after ingest has run dual-path for 15 trading days. Rahul can put that on a roadmap. I will not hide a cutover inside a lister design.
2. Why the source looks like this

Clearhaven clears through RailClear. RailClear's settlement drop is a batch of pipe-delimited files, one per relationship, named RC_{rel}_{yyyymmdd}_{seq}.stl. Typical day: 146 to 210 files, 1.8 to 4.6 GB uncompressed, gzipped in the bucket. They land under s3://clh-settlement-prod/inbound/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd}/. A 'landing' is the S3 PUT completing, not the last byte of a multipart that is still open. Lena Ortiz, who owns the RailClear file contract on their side, says they finish the PUT and then write a sibling .ok object. We will wait for the .ok. If we read the .stl before .ok we have already done that, in October 2022, and we parsed a truncated file, and Helen still mentions it.

There is no RailClear Postgres, Oracle, or SQL Server we are allowed to touch. I asked. Marcus asked. Lena asked her people. The answer in the January 11 email is 'files are the interface.' Debezium needs a WAL or a binlog or at least a table. We do not have one. Building a fake table by loading files into a staging database just so Debezium can read them is a cartoon. Chris said that in the meeting and he was right.
2.1 What today does, so we know what we are replacing

Today a cron on nas-clh-01 mounts the bucket via a Goofys hack Diego hates, copies new .stl files to /data/settlement/inbound, and fires a Python parser that writes CSV into match-engine's back door. Lag on a normal day is 12-40 minutes after the last .ok. On a late RailClear night it is 'whenever someone notices.' There is no hash. Re-copying a file double-posts breaks. That is the November 2022 mess that got us the recon platform work. This design exists so that double-post has to fight a primary key.

blocks.text: 3. Why not Debezium

This section is here because the idea will come back the first time someone new joins and sees 'CDC' in a title. CDC in this document means 'change from the file landing,' not 'change from a database.' The title is a little wrong. I am keeping it because the ticket is already named CLH-TDD-2023-002 and because Marcus uses CDC in TAM slides. If you are searching for Debezium, read this and then stop.

items: No source database. RailClear will not give us a replica. Lena confirmed January 11, 2023. A connector with no slot to create is not a connector.

Staging-DB-plus-Debezium was sketched by a well-meaning architect on a whiteboard on January 9. Load files into Postgres, set replica identity, connect Debezium, emit to Kafka. That gives us two writers to the staging DB (the loader and whoever 'fixes' a row), a WAL we now have to operate, and a connector whose order is the load order, which is the list order, which we already have without the database. We would own a Postgres cluster for the privilege of ignoring it.

Debezium heartbeat, snapshot, and schema-history topics are real operational load. Diego does not want another Kafka Connect cluster on this account while we are still stabilizing clh-kafka-prod. We have six brokers and they are busy with match.
File schema drift is a parser problem. Debezium would still need the loader to type the columns. The hard part does not move.
License and Connect workers are not free. Even the open connector wants machines and a human. The lister is one Deployment, 1 vCPU, 1 Gi, plus a 20-line SQL table.

blocks.text: I am not running Connect so I can CDC a table I just loaded from the file I already had.

Later maybe. If RailClear opens a relational feed in 2024, we write a new design and we can talk Debezium or a native logical slot then. We do not reserve topic names for that future today, except we keep clh.settlement.inbound as the contract so a future source can publish the same Avro. That is the only concession to later.
4. Lister plus hash
4.1 What the lister does

clh-file-lister is a Java service because ingest is Java and Kavya does not want a third runtime in this path yet. It runs in ns clh-prod, one pod, then two if we need HA (leader election on a Postgres advisory lock, not etcd, we are not adding a DCS for a lister). Loop: list prefix inbound/{today}/ and inbound/{yesterday}/ (yesterday because late files), filter .stl objects that have a sibling .ok, HEAD for size and etag, GET the body if we have not stored the hash, SHA-256, compare to ingest.file_index, produce or skip, write file_index if produce succeeded. Sleep 8 seconds. Also subscribe to S3 Event Notification on ObjectCreated:* as a hint to wake early. The hint is not trusted. S3 events drop. The list is the source of truth.

-- ingest.file_index, applied by CLH-TCK-5119
CREATE TABLE ingest.file_index (
  content_sha256   CHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
  bucket           TEXT NOT NULL,
  object_key       TEXT NOT NULL,
  etag             TEXT NOT NULL,
  bytes            BIGINT NOT NULL,
  settlement_dt    DATE NOT NULL,
  filename         TEXT NOT NULL,
  first_seen_at    TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  produced_at      TIMESTAMPTZ,
  kafka_topic      TEXT,
  kafka_partition  INT,
  kafka_offset     BIGINT,
  late             BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
  UNIQUE (bucket, object_key, etag)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_file_index_dt ON ingest.file_index (settlement_dt, late);
blocks.caption: Idempotency table. Hash is the PK because RailClear reuses filenames on a resend. Object_key+etag is unique so a same-name different-body resend is a new row.

blocks.text: Hash is SHA-256 of the decompressed body if Content-Encoding or the key ends in .gz, else of the raw bytes. Lena said they will start gzipping mid-Q1. If we hash the gzip envelope, a recompress of the same rows looks like a new file and we double-post. Decompress first. I will put a 64 MB cap on in-memory decompress and spill to /tmp above that. Biggest file we have seen is 86.4 MB gzipped, 412 MB raw (rel=CLH-PRIME, 2022-12-16). The lister pod gets 2 Gi if we go there, not 1 Gi.
4.2 What the lister does not do

items: Does not parse settlement rows. Does not know a CUSIP from a quantity. Chris's parser in ingest does that, already, against the NAS path. We reuse it.
Does not delete from S3. Lifecycle rule on the bucket is 35 days, Diego's ticket. Lister is not a janitor.
Does not write to match-engine. Kafka only.
Does not 'fix' a bad .ok. If .ok exists and body is truncated, we still hash and produce, and ingest DLQs the parse. Better a DLQ than a silent skip. Helen can see a DLQ. She cannot see a skip.
Does not run in RailClear's account. Their bucket is theirs. Ours is a copy they push with a role we own. If the push stops, lister idles. Alert on zero files by 20:15 ET on a trading day.

blocks.text: 5. Schema and topic contract

Topic clh.settlement.inbound. Avro subject clh.settlement.inbound-value, compatibility BACKWARD. Key is a string, not Avro, so the console tools keep working. 24 partitions. That is less than clh.match.inbound on purpose. Settlement is hundreds of files, not millions of events. The events inside the file explode in ingest, not in the lister. One Kafka record per file, not per row. Per-row would make the lister a parser.

{
  "type": "record",
  "name": "SettlementFileLanding",
  "namespace": "clh.settlement",
  "fields": [
    {"name": "content_sha256", "type": "string"},
    {"name": "bucket", "type": "string"},
    {"name": "object_key", "type": "string"},
    {"name": "etag", "type": "string"},
    {"name": "bytes", "type": "long"},
    {"name": "settlement_dt", "type": "string", "doc": "ISO date, from filename, not from S3 mtime"},
    {"name": "filename", "type": "string"},
    {"name": "rel_code", "type": "string"},
    {"name": "seq", "type": "int"},
    {"name": "late", "type": "boolean"},
    {"name": "ok_found", "type": "boolean"},
    {"name": "listed_at", "type": "long", "doc": "epoch millis ET-normalized timestamp we listed"},
    {"name": "s3_last_modified", "type": "long"},
    {"name": "schema_hint", "type": ["null", "string"], "default": null}
  ]
}
blocks.caption: Avro for one landing. schema_hint is reserved for the day RailClear adds a header row. Do not put parsed trades in this record.

blocks.text: 5.1 Ordering

Kafka preserves order per partition. We set key = settlement_dt + '|' + filename so a resend of the same name on the same day hits the same partition and the consumer sees the second landing after the first. We do not globally order files across relationships. Rel CLH-PRIME and rel CLH-ADVANTAGE can parse in parallel. match-engine already matches per account, not per file. People who want a total order of the bucket listing are asking for a single partition. We will not give them a single partition. 24 is already more than the 4 ingest pods can use; we are matching the number Sneha asked for so tests can pin keys.

Inside a file, row order is RailClear's. Ingest must not sort. If RailClear sends a cancel after an open in the same file, that order is load-bearing. Chris's parser emits Kafka messages on clh.match.inbound with keys acct_id, and those messages keep the file order only within the same acct_id partition. Cross-account reorder is allowed. Same-account reorder is not. That rule already exists in CLH-TDD-2022-021. The lister does not change it. The lister never sees rows.
5.2 Idempotency

file_index.content_sha256 is the gate. Produce is after the INSERT attempt. If two lister pods both see a new file (advisory lock failed, or a bug), both will try INSERT. One wins. The loser skips produce. If produce succeeds and the process dies before UPDATE of kafka_offset, we may produce twice with the same hash. Downstream ingest must treat content_sha256 as idempotent too. That is a UNIQUE on ingest.raw_event(content_sha256) where source_topic = clh.settlement.inbound. Kavya adds that constraint in the same ticket as the table. A duplicate Kafka record is a no-op insert, not a second parse.
6. Late files after 8pm

Helen's desk treats 20:00 ET as the line between 'settlement arrived' and 'settlement is late.' RailClear's contract with Clearhaven says 19:30 ET with a 30 minute grace, which is how we got 20:00. Reality: in November and December 2022, 14 of 42 trading days had at least one file with .ok after 20:00. Median late offset was 22.4 minutes. Worst was 01:16 ET the next calendar day (2022-12-16, CLH-PRIME, the 412 MB file). We cannot drop those files. We also cannot pretend they were on time. late=true is the flag. It is set if listed_at is after 20:00 America/New_York on settlement_dt, not if S3 last_modified is after 20:00, because last_modified moves on a copy.
6.1 Rules

items: Files with .ok before 20:00 ET: late=false. Normal path. ingest parses, match-engine includes them in the day's slices.

Files with .ok after 20:00 and before 02:00 ET next calendar day: late=true. ingest parses. match-engine includes them in a late slice named slice_late_{settlement_dt}. Helen's terminal already has a banner for late slices from the NAS world. Keep the banner.

Files with .ok after 02:00 ET: still produce, still parse, still late=true. Page Helen and page on-call. Do not auto-include in the next day's open. A 02:00+ file is often a correction of a file we already hashed. If the hash differs, it is a new landing and ingest must run the correction path (CLH-TCK-5204, Chris). If the hash matches, it is a re-PUT and we skip.
A file that lands before 20:00 but whose .ok is missing until 20:40: we wait for .ok. We do not parse on size-stable heuristics. October 2022. Do not repeat it.

A day with zero files by 20:15 ET: page. Could be a holiday we forgot, could be RailClear down, could be the IAM role. Lena is on the holiday calendar. Check that before you call her at 20:16 on MLK day. This design ships January 19. MLK is Monday.

blocks.caption: Late-file matrix. 02:00 is Priya's number from January 18. Helen wanted 00:30. We pushed to 02:00 because December 16 would have paged at 00:30 while the file was still a legitimate RailClear late, not a correction.

blocks.text: Timezone is America/New_York. Listed_at is stored as timestamptz. The 20:00 cutoff uses AT TIME ZONE, not a UTC clock. DST in March will try to kill us if someone writes a UTC comparison. Sneha gets a test that freezes 2023-03-12 01:59 and 03:01. I will write it if she does not.
7. Failure modes
7.1 Truncated body with a present .ok

RailClear has done this twice in the last year. Lister will hash the truncated body, produce, ingest will DLQ the parse. Operator path: tell Lena, wait for a resend with a new body (new hash), let the new landing through. Do not delete the file_index row of the truncated hash. That row is evidence. The new hash is a new row. If you delete the old hash and they resend the truncated body again, we would produce the poison file a second time.
7.2 Lister down for 40 minutes

List loop is every 8 seconds but a dead pod misses nothing permanently because S3 still holds the objects. On restart we list today and yesterday. Worst case we mark a file late that arrived on time, if we restarted after 20:00. That is a false late, which is annoying and better than a miss. Alert on lister uptime, not on 'did I list in the last 8 seconds' only. Two pods with advisory lock: the follower lists nothing. If the leader dies, lock expires in 30 seconds (we will set it). Do not set it to 5 minutes. 5 minutes plus 20:00 is a false-late factory.
7.3 Hash collision

SHA-256 collision on a settlement file is not a thing we design around. I am not writing a fallback CRC. If Chris wants a second hash later, it is an added column, not a blocker. The unique (bucket, object_key, etag) exists so a same-hash different-key curiosity would still be visible. I do not expect to see it.
7.4 Kafka unavailable

Lister does not INSERT file_index as produced until the produce ack (acks=all, we can afford it at file rate). If Kafka is down, the loop skips produce, does not write produced_at, retries next pass. Same file, same hash, still not in the table as produced. Do not buffer files on local disk as a sidecar queue. The bucket is the queue. Local disk on a lister pod is how we lose a file on a reschedule.
7.5 Parser slower than landing

One 412 MB file can take ingest 6.8 minutes to explode into clh.match.inbound (Chris measured on 2022-12-16 replay). Lister will be 'done' in 20 seconds. Lag will show on ingest, not on the lister. Do not scale lister when Helen asks why match is late at 20:22. Look at ingest CPU and the parse time histogram. This is the same confusion we already have with the NAS cron finishing early.
7.6 Dual-path with NAS during cutover

For 15 trading days we will run NAS cron and lister in parallel. file_index does not stop the NAS parser. Dual-write into match is the danger. During dual-path, NAS parser writes to a side table, not to breaks.break_open. Comparison job is Chris's. If someone 'helps' by pointing NAS at the prod breaks table during dual-path, we double-post again. SOP will say it. I am saying it here too.
8. What we will not build

Lambda per object. Cold start plus VPC ENI on this account is 12-40 seconds, which is embarrassing next to an 8 second list loop, and debugging Lambda in a settlement incident at 21:00 is worse than kubectl logs. S3 Select. Nice demo, does not give us a Kafka contract. Kinesis Firehose from S3. Wrong shape. Spark streaming on the bucket. Chris wants Spark for backfill later (that will be its own TDD). Not for the 19:40 landing. A 'schema registry for the pipe-delimited rows' inside the lister. No. The landing record is the schema. The row schema lives in ingest.

Rejected alternative, restated so it has a heading: Debezium on a staging database we load from S3. Died January 13. Reasons in section 3. If a vendor slide shows up in a steering deck in March, send them this document.
9. Engineer build notes

items: Repo: clh-file-lister, Java 17, same parent POM as ingest. Kavya will review the POM. Do not add Spring Cloud AWS if the S3 SDK v2 plus a 40-line loop will do.
IAM: role clh-file-lister-prod, read-only on s3://clh-settlement-prod/inbound/*. No delete. No write. Write goes to Kafka and to ingest.file_index via the clh_ingest user.
Config: LIST_INTERVAL_MS=8000, PREFIXES=inbound/{yyyy}/{mm}/{dd} computed in ET, WAIT_FOR_OK=true, CUTOFF_HOUR=20, SALVAGE_HOUR=2, ADVISORY_LOCK_ID=5119.

Metrics: files_listed, files_produced, files_skipped_hash, files_waiting_ok, last_ok_age_seconds, late_files_total. Datadog dashboard clh-settlement-lister. Page on last_ok_age_seconds > 900 on a trading day after 16:00, and on zero produced by 20:15.

Produce: acks=all, linger.ms=5, max.request.size=6 MiB (the Avro is small; the cap is belt). Do not put the file body in the Kafka record. Put the hash and the key. Ingest reads S3 itself. Duplicating 412 MB into Kafka is a tax we will not pay.
Tests: Sneha gets a MinIO fixture with 3 files, one missing .ok, one duplicate hash, one late timestamp. Nightly, not only on PR.
Rollout: shadow bucket clh-settlement-shadow first, 5 trading days, then prod dual-path, then NAS cron off. Dual-path start target February 10. NAS off target March 3 if the comparison job is boring.

blocks.text: 10. Open questions

rows: Will RailClear start gzipping in Q1 and will they tell Lena the week before?
If they flip without notice, our decompress cap is the breaker.
24 partitions or 12? 24 is for Sneha's pin tests more than for throughput.
I can live with 12. Changing later is a new topic.
Who owns the 15-day dual-path comparison job?
Needs a ticket. Suggested CLH-TCK-5204 sibling.
Is 02:00 salvage too late for Helen's cash desk?
She asked for 00:30. Priya held 02:00. Helen should see a week of December data.
Do we need a second bucket for corrections vs inbound?
Lena says corrections reuse inbound/. A second prefix would be nicer. We may not get it.
Advisory lock in Postgres vs a k8s lease?
I picked Postgres because the table is already there. He may want a Lease object.
blocks.caption: Open questions. Helen's 02:00 question is the one that can still change the matrix in section 6.

blocks.text: 11. Calendar and cost

Build is me, two weeks, overlapping Kavya's review. Chris has three days of parser wiring and the unique constraint. Sneha has a week of MinIO fixtures. Diego has a day of IAM and the lifecycle rule. Shadow Kafka already exists. New topic is a config change, not a broker buy. Cost: one extra pod, maybe two, on the existing cluster, plus a few GB of file_index. The 412 MB file stays in S3, not in Kafka. If we had put bodies in the topic, 210 files * a few hundred MB would have been a storage conversation with Diego. We are not having that conversation.

March 3 prod target assumes RailClear does not change the filename layout. If they add a header row, schema_hint gets a value and ingest branches. If they add a new rel_code, nothing in the lister cares, ingest might. Lena will forward the notice. If the notice comes as a file that fails parse, that is also a notice.
